docs.title: I. Home
docs.text:
Last updated: 25 Nov 2026

Technical documentation of the snowpackbc tool chain: AWSOME (Avalanche Warning Service Operational Model Environment) set up for four western Canadian operations, run daily in AWS and published on snowpackbc.com.

This site is for modellers and developers: what data comes in, which script does what, how SNOWPACK is configured, and how the output is post-processed and checked against observations. To read the dashboard, see the AWSOME BC User Guide.

docs.title: VI. AvAPro
docs.text:
Last updated: 25 Nov 2026

AvAPro (Avalanche Problem) derives avalanche problems (storm slab, wind slab, persistent, deep persistent, wet) from simulated snow profiles. It started as Ben Reuter's Matlab code for avalanche-problem climatologies, was translated to Python at the Tyrolean avalanche warning service (supervision Christoph Mitterer; Michi Binder and Martin Perfler), and was extended for North America (v2). v3 (avapro_xs) brings it onto xsnow for the snowpackbc chain.

Version Code Input Status v1 main .pro / .smet, one weak layer at a time, daily 06 h / 15 h baseline v2 py-code/, branch hourly-find-aps .pro / .smet of point runs (AWS and HRDPS-at-station), flat + 8 aspects reference, used for the ISSW 2026 validation v3 avapro_xs/, branch avapro-v3 xsnowpack.zarr of any AWSOME node (hex, grid, station; 5 or 9 slopes; any Δt) in development

More on v1/v2: Documentation_ISSW → AvaPro v1 / v2.

docs.title: 1. Method (v2)
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  P["SNOWPACK profiles<br/>flat + 38° slopes"] --> D["Detection (find_aps)"]
  D --> BW["Burial window<br/>hn24 > 5 cm"]
  D --> RTA["RTA scan<br/>RTA ≥ 0.7"]
  D --> WS["WSAP<br/>wind + surface grains"]
  D --> WA["WAP<br/>LWC / isothermal"]
  BW -->|persistent grains| PAP["PAP stack"]
  BW -->|other interface| NAP["NAP stack"]
  RTA -->|near ground ≤ 20 cm<br/>or slab > 80 cm| DAP["DAP stack"]
  RTA -->|else| PAP
  NAP & PAP & DAP --> M["Layer metrics<br/>INI · PRO · DAM"]
  M --> A["Assignment (post_processing)<br/>trigger / natural per member, OR over members"]
  WS --> A
  WA --> A
  A --> E["Early PAP → NAP<br/>(recent storm load ≥ WL depth)"]
  E --> AMPM["AM [6,12) / PM [12,18)<br/>local time"]

Figure 1. AvAPro v2: detection, stacks, assignment, AM/PM product.

docs.title: 1.1 Detection
docs.text:
Detector Problem Rule NAP Storm slab burial window (once a day when hn24 > 5 cm) finds a new interface; kept while new snow / 48 h snow / slab criteria hold (nsthrsh 0.2 m, minSLthrsh 0.20 m, minSLdens 120 kg m⁻³); kept 3 days from burial, then only while it passes INI and PRO PAP Persistent slab burial window over persistent grains (SH, FC, FCxr, DH, …), or the daily RTA scan (RTA ≥ 0.7) DAP Deep persistent RTA-found persistent layer near the ground (≤ 20 cm) or under a deep slab (> 80 cm); own stack, PAP thresholds WSAP Wind slab VW_drift ≥ vw_thrsh in the past 24 h with suitable surface grains; persists up to vw_thrsh_days = 3 WAP Wet snow LWC thresholds (lwcthrsh 0.008, lwcthrsh_0 0.01, lwcthrsh_1 0.03) and isothermal age ≤ dysisomax

PAP, NAP and DAP are stacks: several members per step; near-duplicates within 0.3 m are merged; a day flag is the OR over members.

docs.title: 1.2 Layer metrics and assignment
docs.text:
Metric Meaning INI initiation: weak-layer strength vs. skier load (SNOWPACK τp, CoJ15 ageing at night) PRO propagation: critical crack length (Gaume et al. 2017 / van Herwijnen et al. 2016) DAM natural release: load added since burial Mode Rule Trigger INI ≤ thr and PRO ≤ thr (NaN does not pass) Natural trigger and DAM ≤ thr NAP thresholds effectively open → existence-driven PAP / DAP thresholds INI 1.31, PRO 0.42, DAM 18

Early PAP → NAP: a PAP that passes the trigger test is assigned as storm slab if the recent storm sum (last 3 days of hn24, extended up to 7 days while hn24 > 5 cm) is at least its weak-layer depth. On that AM/PM slot the PAP flag is cleared.

docs.title: 1.3 Product
docs.text: Hourly internally, published as AM [6, 12) and PM [12, 18) local time, OR over the hours. For daily InfoEx nowcasts: calendar-day OR(AM, PM). See Observations & Assessments.

docs.title: 2.1 Goal
docs.text: One code path for every AWSOME store, any number of aspects, any time step, and North American or European problem sets from the .ini. Output: problems per location, slope and step, plus the dashboard key snowpack.avalanche_problem.

docs.title: 2.2 Stages
docs.text: Stage Module What 1 Load load.py open store, select slopes by coordinate, Δt, local time, forecast mask; band and region_id from locations.json 2 Normalise normalise.py slope-normal geometry (× cos inclination), grain families, units, burial time per layer, rebuilt HN on 06 UTC dump steps 3 Profile series profile.py hn24, hn48, drift, HS, 24 h VW max, evaluated flag, days without load, storm sum A Layer metrics stage_a.py slab depth, density, E; τp, τg, σg; INI; PRO; candidates (stateless, vectorised) B Tracking stage_b.py, stage_b_metrics.py, stage_b_states.py detection, member registry, keep/drop, CoJ15 ageing, DAM since burial, WSAP timer, WAP state C Assignment stage_c.py trigger/natural per member, early PAP → NAP, OR over members, approach profile D Publish publish.py, manifest.py AM/PM, aspect sectors, region × band, zarr + parquet + dashboard key

docs.title: 2.3 Status (25 Nov 2026)
docs.text: Phase Status Config, load, normalise, profile series, 12 node configs done Stage A (layer metrics) done Stage B1–B4 (metrics, v2 registry with exact v2 parity on 32 runs, deposition-date tracking, WSAP/WAP) done Stage C (assignment) next Bridge test SC7a (v3 v2_compat reproduces v2 AM/PM flags) to do Stage D (publish), daily pipeline step to do

docs.title: 2.4 Configuration
docs.text:
config_files/v3/base_north_america.ini      thresholds, approach profiles, [behaviour]
config_files/v3/nodes/<op>_<hex|grid|stn>.ini   [node] store, band_source, band table; timezone, slope_aspects, ...

No overrides: a key set in both files is an error. Each run records the sha256 of both files.

Approach Problems Labels north_america NAP, WSAP, PAP, DAP, WAP Storm Slab, Wind Slab, Persistent Slab, Deep Persistent Slab, Loose Wet / Wet Slab europe (skeleton, not calibrated) same detectors, DAP → PAP New Snow, Wind-Drifted Snow, Persistent Weak Layers, Wet Snow

[behaviour] switches cover every known v2 issue; the preset v2_compat reproduces v2, v3_default is the corrected behaviour. The base config runs preset = v2_compat until bridge test SC7a passes. Examples:

Switch v2_compat v3_default tracking v2_height deposition_date (a member follows its date group; merges re-attach within 48 h) instab_mode v2_daynight every step hour_clock utc local rb15_slope_correction double (cos² on 38°) single

Time zones come from the pinned tzdata package (IANA 2026f), never from the system, so laptop and worker agree.

docs.title: 2.5 Output (planned)
docs.text:
Output Location avaprob.zarr /opt/awsome/<node>/avapro/ (same location × time × slope coords as xsnow) members.parquet one row per tracked layer per step manifest.json config hashes, tzdata, date_opera, store path dashboard key snowpack.avalanche_problem in every feature of <node>/geojson/<stamp>.<aspect>.json: storm_slab, wind_slab, wet_snow, persistent, deep_persistent

The dashboard already has the Avalanche Problem filter as a placeholder (dcfg_semi.add_problem_filter). The daily step will run after geojson_extras.py and before dcfg_semi.py, inside the AWSOME Python, recomputing the full season every day.

Experimental

Until the validation phase on the xsnow chain, every v3 output is labelled experimental. The v2 validation (NAP@TL, WAP@TL, PAP@ALP, WSAP@ALP at point sites) does not carry over to hexagons, grid cells or 4-aspect runs without the bridge tests.

docs.title: 2.6 Development
docs.text: Each change runs through /v3-cycle: a developer agent implements, then code-reviewer, snowpack-expert and scientific-reviewer check it against docs/v3/RULES.md; every cycle is logged in docs/v3/REVIEW_LOG.md. Method changes against v2 are listed in docs/v3/METHOD_CHANGES.md.

docs.title: VII. Observations & Assessments
docs.text:
Last updated: 25 Nov 2026

The model chain runs on weather input only. Field observations and forecaster assessments come in on a separate, offline path: they are the reference the simulations and AvAPro are checked against. Two sources are used:

Source What Access InfoEx (Canadian Avalanche Association) operational hazard assessments, avalanche problems, avalanche observations, weak-layer tracking, snowpack summaries of the four operations read-only database replica, infoex Python package Avalanche Canada public forecasts (danger ratings per band, problems) for Banff, Whistler, Rogers Pass, MWHS regions downloaded per season

The weather-station observations that drive the Stations configuration are described under Weather Input §7.

Confidential data

InfoEx is industry information exchange between operations, not a public bulletin. This page describes the data types and the processing only; no InfoEx content is published here or on the dashboard.

docs.title: 1. Flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  DB[("InfoEx<br/>read replica")] -->|infoex download| RP[("raw parquet<br/>hazard assessments<br/>avalanche problems")]
  DB -->|validation.download_wp2| RW[("raw WP2 tables")]
  RW -->|validation.build_wp2| T[("processed WP2 tables<br/>ha · presence · layers · avalanches")]
  AC["Avalanche Canada<br/>forecasts"] --> PR["processing.prepare_avcan"]
  RP --> DS["processing.daily_summary"]
  DS --> PL["plots: danger levels,<br/>problems, InfoEx vs AvCan"]
  PR --> PL
  T --> V["Validation<br/>AvAPro / SNOWPACK"]
  AV["AvAPro AM/PM<br/>problems"] --> V
  XS["xsnow profiles<br/>datetags"] --> V

Figure 1. From InfoEx and Avalanche Canada to the validation tables.

docs.title: 2. The infoex package
docs.text:
Python tools for downloading and analysing InfoEx data. Credentials come only from environment variables / .env (or the system keychain), the package only reads, and always from the read replica.

Module Content db.py connection settings and SQLAlchemy engine, check_connection operations.py operation catalog, search, registry of slugs (banff_n, blackcomb, glacier_n, mike_wieg) locations.py location layers (operating area, zones, runs, weather sites) → GeoJSON hazard.py hazard assessments, ratings per band, avalanche problems, weak layers (pwl, pwl_assessment) observations.py avalanche observations (with aspect/elevation flags and location centroids), daily avalanche summary, snowpack summaries validation.py WP2 validation tables inventory.py completeness checks: table inventory, fill rates, links, daily coverage processing.py daily_hazard, daily_summary, prepare_avcan plotting.py danger levels, problems overview, InfoEx vs Avalanche Canada cli.py infoex command 
infoex check                                       # test the connection
infoex operations Whistler                         # search the operation catalog
infoex download --ops all --seasons 2024/25 2025/26
infoex layers --ops banff_n --layers OpArea Zones  # GeoJSON
infoex available                                   # operation x season on disk
Operation InfoEx slug Model operation Banff National Park (north) banff_n Banff Whistler Blackcomb blackcomb Whistler Glacier National Park (north) glacier_n Rogers Pass Mike Wiegele Heliskiing mike_wieg MWHS

Seasons run 1 Nov – 30 May. Data from 2021/22 to 2025/26 is on disk.

docs.title: 3.1 Hazard assessments
docs.text: One row per assessment, character = nowcast or forecast, with per band (alp_, tl_, btl_): danger rating (hzd), confidence, stability, comment. daily_hazard keeps one assessment per day (the latest with a danger rating).

docs.title: 3.2 Avalanche problems
docs.text:
Rows of the problem table with the problem type, nowcast/forecast, the aspects per elevation band, and the hazard chart (likelihood × size). Problem types are mapped to one vocabulary:

InfoEx character Summary column STORM_SLAB Storm Slab WIND_SLAB Wind Slab PERSISTENT_SLAB Persistent Slab DEEP_PERSISTENT_SLAB Deep Persistent Slab LOOSE_DRY_AVALANCHE / DRY_LOOSE Dry Loose LOOSE_WET_AVALANCHE / WET_LOOSE Wet Loose WET_SLAB Wet Slab CORNICE / CORNICE_FALL Cornice GLIDE_AVALANCHE / GLIDE Gliding

The hazard chart is parsed to size and likelihood on the 1–5 scales (1 + 0.5 · value, checked against depth and sensitivity).

docs.title: 3.3 Observations
docs.text: Table Use Avalanche observations date, size, trigger, aspect × elevation flags, location centroid; linked to weak layers where reported Avalanche summary daily avalanches_observed, percent_area_observed (observation effort) Weak layers + layer assessments layer name (e.g. Jan 26 SH/MFcr/FC → burial date + grain types), status over time, depth, bands Snowpack summaries free text with weak-layer links; context only

docs.title: 4.1 WP2 tables (grid configuration work plan §6)
docs.text:
notebooks/05_wp2_validation_data.ipynb builds the tables for one operation and season:

from infoex import validation, inventory
raw = validation.download_wp2(engine, "glacier_n", "2025/26")
tables = validation.build_wp2(raw, "2025/26", character="nowcast")
validation.save_wp2(tables, "glacier_n", "2025/26")
inventory.requirements_check(tables)
Table Grain ha date × band × problem ha_bands date × band: danger rating, confidence, stability ha_presence dense date × band × aspect × problem (0 = not listed, NaN = no assessment) layer_assessments, layers_daily weak-layer status per day, listed in an assessment, avalanches on the layer layers_lookup one row per relevant weak layer (+ CSV for the manual match to model datetags) avalanches record × band aai_daily, obs_effort avalanche activity index, observation effort

docs.title: 4.2 Matching model and truth
docs.text:
As in the v2 point validation (ISSW 2026):

Model InfoEx truth Band NAP (storm slab) Storm Slab TL WSAP (wind slab) Wind Slab ALP PAP (persistent) Persistent Slab ALP WAP (wet) Wet Loose / Wet Slab TL
  • InfoEx nowcast problems are the truth; danger levels by band are context and filters.
  • Model days before the first InfoEx day of the season are dropped (no truth).
  • Daily InfoEx vs. AM/PM model: y_pred = OR(AM, PM) of the calendar day.
  • Scores: day-exact and timing-tolerant contingency scores on the InfoEx-aligned window.

docs.title: 4.3 For the xsnow chain (next)
docs.text:
• The v2 validation was at point sites (station elevation = the InfoEx truth band). Hexagon × band and grid cells have their own model band from locations.json, so "validated" is redefined once the whole xsnow pipeline exists.
  • Weak layers: InfoEx layer names (burial date) against the model's datetags per region × band.
  • Avalanche observations with aspect × elevation flags against the slope-resolved problems.
  • Avalanche Canada forecasts as a second, public reference.

docs.title: IV. SNOWPACK
docs.text:
Last updated: 25 Nov 2026

SNOWPACK (SLF) is run by AWSOME's atoolchain inside the awsome container, once per node and day. The recipe decides what is simulated (locations, slopes, sources, post-processing); the SNOWPACK ini comes from AWSOME's profsnow templates (flavour nwp), with per-point snippets from our SMET generators.

docs.title: 1. Run setup (recipe)
docs.text:
All three recipes share the same snowpack section (configs/hex_v2_recipe.yaml, anchor &snowpack):

run:
  season_start: "2026-10-04"     # HRDPS archive start
  season_end:   "2027-05-31"
  date_opera:   now              # daily run: --date-opera <day>T06:00
  ncpus: 2
terrain:
  aspects: [N, E, S, W]          # stations: N NE E SE S SW W NW
  angles:  [38]                  # flat is added automatically
snowpack:
  flavor: nwp
  flavor-pre: nwp-pre
  resume: true
  restart: false
  allow_partial: true
  output_format: zarr
  snippets: /ext_awsome/<config>/smet/snippets
Key Meaning flavor / flavor-pre ini templates nwp.ini (paths, slopes) on top of nwp-pre.ini (physics, output, filters) resume: true every run continues from the saved .sno state (<node>/snow-nowcast/) restart: false no cold start unless the state is missing allow_partial: true a failing location does not fail the node output_format: zarr SNOWPACK's ZarrIO plugin writes snowpack.zarr (needs the feat/zarr-plugin-aw build) snippets per-point ini fragments: PSUM::GENERATOR1 = CST 0 (see below)

docs.title: 1.1 Data sources per node
docs.text:
Same pattern as AWSOME's gridded.yaml, all three read our SMET folders through adatahub's built-in local SMET source (source: smet, provider: point):

Source Role Window Purpose history backfill season season-to-date nowcast; no-op once covered nowcast update operational, days_past: 3 rewinds 3 days so the analysis overwrites yesterday's forecast hours forecast update operational, days_past: 0, lead_time: 2 06Z run, +48 h

A season-mode update would only extend from the hub cursor, which sits at the end of the previous forecast: the resume would then never replace forecast hours with analysis. Hence the operational nowcast source.

docs.title: 1.2 Locations and bands
docs.text: locations.builder: geojson reads the generator's locations.geojson (Point, station_id, altitude); the region comes from regions.geojson by point-in-polygon; bands from elevation_bands {edges, names} (points below the first edge are dropped). The SMET station_id and the location id must be identical: the hub merges by label.

docs.title: 2. Daily cycle
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant S as .sno state (yesterday)
  participant N as Nowcast (analysis)
  participant F as Forecast (06Z +48 h)
  participant Z as snowpack.zarr
  S->>N: resume, rewind 3 days
  N->>Z: recompute last 3 days with the newest analysis
  N->>S: save state at <day>T06
  N->>F: copy of the state
  F->>Z: append +48 h forecast

Figure 1. Resume: the nowcast advances the saved state, the forecast runs from a copy.

  • Output every 3 h (PROF_DAYS_BETWEEN = TS_DAYS_BETWEEN = 0.125), first step 4 Oct 01:00.
  • Resume tick (no new data) costs ~13 s per hex node; a cold season run of mwhs_hex took 84 s for SNOWPACK.
  • The 06Z record of each restart is the initial-state dump: HN*, MS_* and wind_trans24 are 0 there (see Weather Input §8).

docs.title: 3. Slopes
docs.text:
Configuration Slopes Semi-distributed, fully gridded flat + 38° N, E, S, W (5) Stations flat + 38° N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW (9)

All slopes use the same weather series (no radiation or wind redistribution by aspect beyond SNOWPACK's own slope radiation). Heights in the output are vertical (m above ground) on every slope.

docs.title: 4. ini: nwp-pre.ini (main settings)
docs.text:
Settings from AWSOME's profsnow/snowpack/templates/nwp-pre.ini. PLACEHOLDER values are filled by atoolchain (coordinates, paths, number of slopes). The worker runs a pinned AWSOME version; check the template there before quoting a value in a paper.

[SNOWPACK][SNOWPACKADVANCED][INTERPOLATIONS1D][FILTERS][GENERATORS] + snippets[OUTPUT] Key Value CALCULATION_STEP_LENGTH 15 min HEIGHT_OF_METEO_VALUES / HEIGHT_OF_WIND_VALUE 2 m / 10 m ROUGHNESS_LENGTH 0.002 m ENFORCE_MEASURED_SNOW_HEIGHTS FALSE → precipitation-driven, no HS assimilation SW_MODE INCOMING ATMOSPHERIC_STABILITY MO_HOLTSLAG CANOPY / SNP_SOIL 0 / FALSE (no soil: layer 0 = bottom snow element) MEAS_TSS / CHANGE_BC FALSE / FALSE Key Value VARIANT / RESEARCH DEFAULT / TRUE SNOW_EROSION / SNOW_REDISTRIBUTION FALSE / FALSE → no wind drift modelled ALLOW_ADAPTIVE_TIMESTEPPING TRUE THRESH_RAIN 1.2 °C FORCE_RH_WATER / THRESH_RH TRUE / 0.5 HOAR_THRESH_TA / _RH / _VW 1.2 °C / 0.97 / 3.5 m/s HOAR_DENSITY_BURIED / HOAR_MIN_SIZE_BURIED / HOAR_DENSITY_SURF 125 kg m⁻³ / 2.0 mm / 100 kg m⁻³ MIN_DEPTH_SUBSURF 0.07 m NEW_SNOW_GRAIN_SIZE 0.3 mm METAMORPHISM_MODEL / STRENGTH_MODEL / VISCOSITY_MODEL DEFAULT WATERTRANSPORTMODEL_SNOW BUCKET ENABLE_VAPOUR_TRANSPORT TRUE SW_ABSORPTION_SCHEME MULTI_BAND HARDNESS_PARAMETERIZATION MONTI HEIGHT_NEW_ELEM / MINIMUM_L_ELEMENT 0.02 m / 0.0025 m COMBINE_ELEMENTS TRUE (merged elements keep the upper deposition date) SSI_IS_RTA / MULTI_LAYER_SK38 TRUE / TRUE (output hacks: SSI column = RTA, SK38 per layer) Field Resampling TA, RH, VW, ISWR LINEAR, extrapolate PSUM ACCUMULATE, period 900 s Field Hard limits Soft limits TA 200–320 K 200–320 K RH 0.01–1.2 0.05–1.0 VW −2–70 m/s 0–50 m/s ISWR / OSWR −10–1500 W m⁻² 0–1500 W m⁻² ILWR 188–600 W m⁻² 200–400 W m⁻² TSG 200–320 K — Field Generator TSG CST 273.15 K (ground at 0 °C) PSUM (snippet, per point) CST 0 → fills the first step, which ACCUMULATE cannot compute after a cold start Key Value PROF_WRITE / TS_WRITE TRUE / TRUE PROF_DAYS_BETWEEN / TS_DAYS_BETWEEN 0.125 d (3 h) PROF_FORMAT PRO in the template; atoolchain switches to the ZarrIO output for output_format: zarr HARDNESS_IN_NEWTON FALSE OUT_HAZ, OUT_STAB, OUT_MASS, OUT_METEO, … TRUE TIME_ZONE 0 (UTC)

docs.title: 5. After SNOWPACK (atoolchain steps)
docs.text:
Step Output Settings xsnowpack xsnowpack.zarr (full layer profiles, see xsnow) chunks: profile indices per-layer stability indices rc_flat, sk38, lwc, punstable, rta, sk38_ccl, sk38_ccl_rta pwl persistent weak layer flags grain types SH, DH, FCxr, FC; FCxr/FC need Punstable ≥ 0.77 datetags layers grouped by the precipitation event that buried them group_by: [region_id, band] simplified simplified.zarr: most critical layer per index, location, slope and time geojson: true dashboard geojson/<stamp>.<aspect>.json (6-hourly, whole season), dcfg/operational.json mode: gridded, display: geojson

Post-processing code: atoolchain, punstable, pwl, datetags, pwet.

docs.title: 6. Run times (t3.large, 2 vCPU)
docs.text:
Node Cold season run Notes mwhs_hex (21 locations × 5 slopes) 2 min 24 s (SNOWPACK 84 s, xsnowpack 38 s) to 3 Nov 2026 whistler_grid (259 cells) 58 min first grid run rogers_grid / banff_grid / mwhs_grid 31 / 42 / 45 min simplified is the slowest step (~8 min per node) station nodes 1.3–1.7 min

Daily runs are incremental (one day + forecast) and much shorter.

docs.title: 7. Commands
docs.text:
# inside the container
atoolchain /ext_awsome/hex_v2/hex_v2_recipe.yaml --toolchain mwhs_hex --date-opera 2026-11-03T00:00
atoolchain <recipe> --dry-run          # plan the steps of every node
atoolchain needs <recipe>              # install requirements

docs.title: II. Tool Chain Overview
docs.text:
Last updated: 25 Nov 2026

One HRDPS download feeds three model configurations. Every configuration runs SNOWPACK through AWSOME's atoolchain, gets the same post-processing, and ends up on the dashboard. Observations and forecaster assessments come in on a separate path and are used to check the model, not to drive it.

docs.title: 1. Flow chart
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  subgraph IN["1 · Weather input"]
    DM["MSC Datamart<br/>HRDPS 2.5 km · RDPS 10 km"] -->|nwp_fetch.py<br/>hourly| RAW[("raw/hrdps · raw/hrdps_precip · raw/rdps<br/>clipped GRIB2 + manifest")]
    RAW -->|hrdps_correct.py| COR[("corrected/hrdps<br/>1664 cells, lapse-rate corrected<br/>+ gust · + MSC snow level")]
    ST["Station feeds<br/>Avalanche Canada · Whistler Blackcomb · Wiegele"] -->|stations_fetch.py<br/>hourly :40| RST[("raw/stations<br/>responses unchanged")]
  end

  subgraph SM["2 · SMET assembly"]
    COR --> HEX["smet_hex_v2.py<br/>hexagon × band median"]
    COR --> GRD["smet_grid.py<br/>one SMET per cell"]
    COR --> STN["smet_stations.py<br/>station obs → HRDPS fill"]
    RST --> STN
  end

  subgraph AT["3 · atoolchain (AWSOME container)"]
    HEX --> LOC
    GRD --> LOC
    STN --> LOC
    LOC["locations · data"] --> SNP["SNOWPACK<br/>flat + 38° slopes, resume"]
    SNP --> XS["xsnowpack<br/>xsnowpack.zarr"]
    XS --> IDX["indices · pwl · datetags"]
    IDX --> SIM["simplified · dashboard<br/>geojson + dcfg"]
  end

  subgraph PP["4 · snowpackbc post-processing"]
    SIM --> EXT["geojson_extras.py<br/>weather filters"]
    XS -.->|planned| AVA["AvAPro v3<br/>avalanche problems"]
    AVA -.-> EXT
    EXT --> DC["dcfg_semi.py<br/>dashboard config"]
  end

  subgraph PUB["5 · Publish"]
    DC -->|site_publish.py| S3[("Site bucket<br/>main · area sites · dev")]
    S3 --> CF["CloudFront<br/>snowpackbc.com"]
    API["Worker: AWSOME API + nivix<br/>/api · /nivix"] --> CF
  end

  subgraph VAL["6 · Observations & assessments (offline)"]
    IX["InfoEx<br/>hazard assessments · problems · avalanches"] --> V["Validation"]
    AC["Avalanche Canada forecasts"] --> V
  end
  AVA -.-> V
  XS -.-> V

Figure 1. The snowpackbc tool chain. Solid lines run every day; dashed lines are planned or offline (AvAPro v3 is in development, validation runs on the analysis machine).

docs.title: 2. Steps in one table
docs.text:
# Step Script / tool Input → output Page 1 Fetch NWP ingest/nwp_fetch.py Datamart → raw/<model>/YYYY/MM/DD/*.grib2 Weather Input 2 Correct pipeline/hrdps_correct.py, pipeline/lapse.py raw GRIB2 → corrected/hrdps/.../HRDPS_<run>_cells.nc Weather Input 2b Side products hrdps_correct.py --gust-pending, pipeline/snlvl_fetch.py → _gust.nc, _snlvl.nc Weather Input 3 Station poll ingest/stations_fetch.py provider pages → raw/stations/... Weather Input 4 SMETs smet_hex_v2.py, smet_grid.py, smet_stations.py corrected cells (+ stations) → <domain>/{nowcast,forecast}/*.smet Weather Input 5 Model atoolchain <recipe> --toolchain <node> SMETs → snowpack.zarr, xsnowpack.zarr, indices, geojson SNOWPACK, xsnow 6 Extras pipeline/geojson_extras.py snowpack.zarr + gust + snow level → weather.* in each geojson feature Weather Input 7 Avalanche problems avapro_xs (v3, in development) xsnowpack.zarr → snowpack.avalanche_problem AvAPro 8 Dashboard config pipeline/dcfg_semi.py dcfg/operational.json (sources, filters, colours, help texts) — 9 Publish pipeline/site_build.py, pipeline/site_publish.py build + geojson + dcfg → site bucket, CloudFront invalidation — 10 Warm + state daily_hex.py steps warm, state pre-load API caches; .sno state and run reports → state/<node>/<day>/ —

The daily orchestrator is pipeline/daily_hex.py: it runs steps 1–10 for the semi-distributed part, then the fully gridded part, then the stations part. Each part has its own success stamp, so a retry repeats only the part that failed, and a problem in the grid never holds back the hexagons.

docs.title: 3. Three configurations
docs.text:
Semi-distributed (hex v2) Fully gridded (grid v1) Stations (stations v1) Recipe configs/hex_v2_recipe.yaml configs/grid_v1_recipe.yaml configs/stations_v1_recipe.yaml Settings configs/hex_v2.yaml configs/grid_v1.yaml configs/stations_v1.yaml Point 15 km hexagon × elevation band one HRDPS 2.5 km cell one weather station Forcing hourly median of the member cells the cell's own corrected series station observation, gaps filled by HRDPS Location id <hex>_<BTL\|TL\|ALP>, e.g. R1_ALP <R\|M\|W\|B>_<i>_<j> station name Region id hexagon label operation (RP-01, MW-01, WH-01, BA-01) 1 km square per station Slopes flat + N/E/S/W at 38° flat + N/E/S/W at 38° flat + 8 aspects at 38° Nodes *_hex *_grid *_stn

One atoolchain node = one configuration of one operation = one output folder /opt/awsome/<node>/.

docs.title: 4. Infrastructure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph AWS["AWS us-east-2"]
    W["Worker EC2 (t3.large)<br/>SSM only, no SSH<br/>systemd timers"]
    C["Docker container 'awsome'<br/>AWSOME install, SNOWPACK, xsnow,<br/>atoolchain, API, nivix"]
    W --- C
    OB[("Ops bucket<br/>code · raw · corrected · logs · state · backup")]
    SB[("Site bucket<br/>www/main · www/dev · area sites")]
    SNS["SNS<br/>alert e-mails"]
    W <--> OB
    W --> SB
    W --> SNS
  end
  SB --> CF["CloudFront<br/>(one distribution per site)"]
  W -->|/api · /nivix| CF
  CF --> U["Browser"]
  MAC["Mac: infra/deploy.sh<br/>code · status · exec"] --> OB
  MAC --> W

Figure 2. Where things run. The worker pulls its code from the ops bucket before every run; the Mac only uploads code and starts commands.

Piece Role infra/stack.yaml CloudFormation: ops bucket, worker EC2 + IAM role, security group, SNS alerts, budget infra/bootstrap.sh Worker setup: micromamba env (eccodes, wgrib2, xarray, …), systemd units and timers, failure alerts infra/awsome_install.sh AWSOME install in the awsome container with pinned commits (versions.json) infra/deploy.sh Run on the Mac: check, up, code, update, status, exec "<cmd>", backfill infra/cloudfront_dev.sh, infra/area_site.sh CloudFront: worker origin for /api/* and /nivix/*; area sites (e.g. banff, mwhs) frontend/build.sh + frontend/*.patch Dashboard frontend (AWSOME's albina-admin-gui) with the snowpackbc patches: semi-distributed display, aspect & elevation rose, weather filters, panel help

Static vs dynamic. The map files (<node>/geojson/*.json, dcfg/*.json, region outlines) are static on S3. The time-series chart (/api/timeseries, AWSOME's dashboard API) and the profile viewer (/nivix/xs*, nivix xserver) need Python services reading the zarr stores, so CloudFront sends those paths to the worker.

docs.title: 5. Schedule
docs.text:
Timer When What NWP fetch hourly at :20 UTC archive every complete HRDPS / RDPS run not yet in raw/ (96 h look-back) Archive status every 30 min status page of the raw archive and the station feeds Station fetch hourly at :40 UTC store every station response unchanged NWP check daily 15:05 UTC e-mail if any run of the last 2 days is missing or incomplete Daily run 03:00 America/Vancouver, retry 05:00 daily_hex.py: hex → grid → stations, publish main + area sites

At 03:00 Pacific the newest complete HRDPS run is 06Z. The day's run uses it as the forecast (06Z + 48 h) and the nowcast up to 06Z (atoolchain --date-opera <day>T06:00). The service runs with low CPU priority (Nice 10), the web services with high priority, and has a 5 h timeout. Any failed step exits 1 and sends an alert e-mail; the site keeps yesterday's data until a run succeeds.

docs.title: 6. Software versions
docs.text:
AWSOME is installed from its GitLab group at pinned commits (recorded in versions.json on the worker and in the ops bucket). Two pins deviate from the defaults (state 3 Nov 2026):

Component Pin Why SNOWPACK branch feat/zarr-plugin-aw (3.7.1+aw) the default deb has no ZarrIO plugin, but output_format: zarr needs it xsnow branch feat/adashboard atoolchain imports ZarrTailSlopeMismatch, which only that branch has

A reinstall must set AWSOME_VERSION_SNOWPACK=feat/zarr-plugin-aw.

docs.title: 7. Repository layout
docs.text: Folder Content ingest/ config.yaml (models, variables, clip box), nwp_fetch.py, nwp_check.py, nwp_status.py, stations.yaml, stations_fetch.py pipeline/ correction, SMET generators, daily_hex.py, geojson_extras.py, dcfg_semi.py, site_build.py, site_publish.py configs/ SMET settings and atoolchain recipes per configuration static/ hexagon polygons (hex_grid_fit_v2/), HRDPS cells (cells/), operation outlines (ops-regions/) infra/ CloudFormation, bootstrap, deploy, CloudFront scripts frontend/ dashboard patches and build script

docs.title: III. Weather Input
docs.text:
Last updated: 25 Nov 2026

Every configuration is driven by the same weather: HRDPS, downloaded once, corrected once to the elevation of each 2.5 km cell, and then assembled into SMET files per model point. The station configuration adds observations from the operations' weather stations on top.

flowchart LR
  A["Datamart<br/>HRDPS GRIB2"] -->|nwp_fetch.py| B[("raw/hrdps<br/>clipped, unchanged")]
  B -->|hrdps_correct.py<br/>lapse.py| C[("corrected/hrdps<br/>_cells.nc")]
  B -->|--gust-pending| G[("_gust.nc")]
  A -->|snlvl_fetch.py| L[("_snlvl.nc")]
  C --> H["smet_hex_v2.py"]
  C --> R["smet_grid.py"]
  C --> S["smet_stations.py"]
  O["station feeds"] -->|stations_fetch.py| OR[("raw/stations")] --> S
  H & R & S --> M["SMET + locations + regions<br/>+ snippets + manifest"]
  G & L --> X["geojson_extras.py"]

Figure 1. Weather data from Datamart to the SNOWPACK input files.

docs.title: 1.1 HRDPS (SNOWPACK forcing)
docs.text:
ECCC/MSC High Resolution Deterministic Prediction System, 2.5 km, continental domain, runs 00/06/12/18Z, hourly leads 0–48. Settings in ingest/config.yaml.

SMET field Datamart file pattern Notes TA _TMP_AGL-2m_ 2 m air temperature RH _RH_AGL-2m_ 2 m relative humidity VW _WIND_AGL-10m_ 10 m wind speed DW _WDIR_AGL-10m_ 10 m wind direction ISWR _DSWRF_Sfc_ incoming shortwave radiation ILWR _DLWRF_Sfc_ incoming longwave radiation PSUM _MSC_HRDPS-WEonG_APCP_Sfc_ precipitation, accumulated since run start GUST (optional) _GUST_AGL-10m_ 10 m gust, dashboard only HGT (optional) _HGT_Sfc_ model orography (lead 0)

A run counts as complete only when every required field exists for every lead.

docs.title: 1.2 Further NWP archives (not used by SNOWPACK yet)
docs.text: Model key What Why hrdps_precip plain HRDPS model precipitation: APCP (since run start), APCP-Accum1h (hourly), PRATE decided as the future PSUM source (instead of WEonG); archived and backfilled to 4 Oct 2026, the switch in hrdps_correct.py is still to do rdps RDPS 10 km, leads 0–84, same variables (long Datamart names, radiation accumulated) day-3 forecast and HRDPS fallback later

docs.title: 1.3 MSC snow level
docs.text: HRDPS-WEonG HGTSNLVL_Sfc (m), read by pipeline/snlvl_fetch.py for the dashboard's comparison filter. It is kept out of the raw archive on purpose: cfgrib may call it unknown, the same name as the WEonG precipitation, so it could end up as PSUM.

docs.title: 2. Download
docs.text:
ingest/nwp_fetch.py, hourly at :20 UTC (systemd timer), 96 h look-back.

  • Source: MSC Datamart, dated tree first (https://dd.weather.gc.ca/{date}/WXO-DD), then the "today" tree. Datamart keeps about 30 days.
  • Clip: BC/Alberta box, lon −132…−110°, lat 48…57°, cut as an index sub-box on the native rotated grid (wgrib2 -ijsmall_grib). Values are not changed.
  • Archive: one file per run in the ops bucket, the same name the old cluster used, so grib2smet.py and later reanalyses read it unchanged:
raw/hrdps/YYYY/MM/DD/HRDPS_YYYYMMDDHH.grib2
raw/hrdps/YYYY/MM/DD/HRDPS_YYYYMMDDHH.manifest.json      <- written last = "run complete"
raw/hrdps_precip/YYYY/MM/DD/HRDPS_PRECIP_YYYYMMDDHH.grib2
raw/rdps/YYYY/MM/DD/RDPS_YYYYMMDDHH.grib2
  • Idempotent: runs whose manifest says complete are skipped. raw/ moves to Glacier Instant Retrieval after 30 days.
  • Checks: ingest/nwp_check.py (daily 15:05 UTC) e-mails when a run of the last two days is missing or incomplete; ingest/nwp_status.py writes a status page every 30 min.
  • Season start: the archive starts 4 Oct 2026, so every simulation cold-starts on that day.
nwp_fetch.py                                   # every run in the look-back window not yet archived
nwp_fetch.py --model hrdps --date 20261102 --run 06
nwp_fetch.py --list hrdps                      # file names Datamart offers (to check the regexes)

docs.title: 3. Correction to cell elevation
docs.text:
pipeline/hrdps_correct.py with pipeline/lapse.py. One archived run in, one NetCDF out:

corrected/hrdps/YYYY/MM/DD/HRDPS_YYYYMMDDHH_cells.nc
  dims (cell, time)   time = valid time of leads 1..48 (hourly values ending at that time)
  vars TA RH VW DW ISWR ILWR PSUM in SMET units (°C, %, m/s, °, W/m², mm/h) + TA_raw, RH_raw

docs.title: 3.1 Points
docs.text:
1664 points = the HRDPS cells of the four operations (static/cells/all_operations_hrdps_corrected.geojson). Each point has

  • z = median MRDEM-30 (NRCan 30 m DEM) of the cell clipped to the operation polygon,
  • z_hrdps = HRDPS model orography at the nearest grid node,
  • dz_hr = z − z_hrdps.

Every generator indexes cells by position, so every corrected file must hold the same cells in the same order. Cells added later are appended at the end (--add-missing-cells), and existing ones stay bit-identical.

docs.title: 3.2 Steps
docs.text:
1. Nearest cell: each point takes the nearest HRDPS grid node.
  2. Units: K → °C. Accumulated fields (stepType=accum: APCP, radiation if delivered as J/m²) are de-accumulated to hourly values; the decision per field is logged and stored in the file attributes.

  3. Lapse-rate correction of TA and RH from z_hrdps to z (same method as Avalanche Canada's grib2smet.py, ported unchanged from the R original; monthly rates after Marsh (2024), Kunkel (1989), Shea et al. (2004)):

    • TA_corr = TA − dz · Γ_T(month)
    • RH via the dew point: RH → vapour pressure (Magnus) → Td → Td_corr = Td − dz · (c/b) · λ(month) → RH from Td_corr and TA_corr.
    • PSUM, radiation and wind are not changed.
Month J F M A M J J A S O N D Γ_T (°C km⁻¹) 4.4 5.9 7.1 7.8 8.1 8.2 8.1 8.1 7.7 6.8 5.5 4.7 λ (km⁻¹) 0.41 0.42 0.40 0.39 0.38 0.36 0.33 0.33 0.36 0.37 0.40 0.40

Figure 2. Lapse-rate correction: peaks get colder, valleys warmer.

RH method: fixed, not grib2smet

The original grib2smet.py adds 273.15 inside the Magnus formula, which expects °C. RH is then inflated even at dz = 0 (−5 °C / 80 % → 94 %) and hardly reacts to dz. snowpackbc uses RH_METHOD=fixed (since 3 Nov 2026): RH stays unchanged at dz = 0. Season median RH went from 92 % to 70 % (raw HRDPS: 70 %); HS changed mostly by 1–2 cm. TA_raw / RH_raw stay in every file, so the old method can always be recomputed for comparison.

hrdps_correct.py --pending              # every archived run without a corrected file (daily run)
hrdps_correct.py --date 20261101 --run 00
hrdps_correct.py --recompute-rh         # rewrite TA/RH of all files from TA_raw/RH_raw

docs.title: 4. Nowcast and forecast stitching
docs.text:
The SMET generators build two hourly series per point from the corrected runs:

Series Rule nowcast each hour t takes the newest run R with 1 ≤ t − R ≤ 6 h (leads 1–6 of the 00/06/12/18Z runs); if that run is missing, the next older run covering t (lead ≤ 48) fills it forecast the day's 06Z run, leads 1–48

Figure 3. Nowcast from the first 6 h of each run, forecast from the 06Z run.

Gaps stop the run

The manifest counts gap_hours (hours no run covers). The daily run stops if gap_hours > 0: the PSUM snippet (§6.4) would otherwise turn missing precipitation into 0 mm.

docs.title: 5. Side products
docs.text:
Not SNOWPACK forcing; used only for the dashboard's weather filters.

Product Script Content HRDPS_<run>_gust.nc hrdps_correct.py --gust-pending 10 m gust (m/s), nearest cell, no correction, leads 1–48 HRDPS_<run>_snlvl.nc snlvl_fetch.py --forecast-run <run> MSC snow level (m) at every cell; NaN where MSC gives a negative code (no precipitation); leads 1–6 per run, 1–48 for the forecast run; only runs still on Datamart (backfilled from 12 Oct 2026)

docs.title: 6. SMET assembly
docs.text:
Three generators, one per configuration, all reading the corrected cells. Each writes per domain:

<config>/smet/<domain>/nowcast/<id>.smet     season-to-date nowcast
<config>/smet/<domain>/forecast/<id>.smet    06Z run, leads 1-48
<config>/smet/<domain>/locations.geojson     one Point per SMET (station_id = SMET id, altitude)
<config>/smet/<domain>/regions.geojson       polygons, id = region_id
<config>/smet/snippets/<id>.ini              per-point SNOWPACK ini snippet
<config>/smet/manifest.json                  period, forecast run, gap_hours, members / donors

The daily run writes into a fresh folder and swaps it in only on success.

docs.title: 6.1 Semi-distributed: smet_hex_v2.py
docs.text:
• Hexagons: static/hex_grid_fit_v2/<op>.geojson (15 km), bands: configs/hex_v2.yaml.
  • A cell belongs to hexagon H and band B if its centre lies in H and its integer altitude lies in B.
  • One point per hexagon × band: the hourly median of the members for TA, RH, VW, ISWR, ILWR, PSUM; a circular mean for DW. Altitude = median member altitude; position = hexagon centre.
  • Id <hex>_<BTL|TL|ALP>, region id = hexagon label.

docs.title: 6.2 Fully gridded: smet_grid.py
docs.text:
• One point per HRDPS cell whose altitude lies inside the operation's bands; cells below the BTL lower limit are not simulated.
  • Id <prefix>_<i>_<j>; region id = the operation (RP-01, MW-01, WH-01, BA-01).
  • Also writes cells.geojson (cell polygons, corners = means of the 2 × 2 grid nodes, ~2.48 × 2.49 km) for the map fill.

docs.title: 6.4 SMET details that matter
docs.text: Detail Why Timestamps naive, header tz = 0 xsnow parses …Z as tz-aware, atoolchain's window is naive → comparison error plot_unit = time ° W/m2 W/m2 mm - K m/s without it xsnow cannot convert RH/TA when staging for SNOWPACK First row on the zarr time grid the zarr time axis starts at season_start; the first row (4 Oct 01:00) must be on its 15 min grid Snippet PSUM::GENERATOR = CST 0 the cold-start .sno takes the first SMET row as profile date, so PSUM ACCUMULATE has no earlier point for the first step. Side effect: any later PSUM gap would become 0 mm (hence the gap rule in §4) EPSG per operation 32610 (Whistler, UTM 10N), 32611 (Rogers, MWHS, Banff, UTM 11N)

docs.title: 7.1 Ingest: stations_fetch.py
docs.text:
Hourly at :40 UTC. Every response is stored unchanged (gzip) so short provider windows are not lost:

raw/stations/<provider>/<station>/YYYY/MM/DD/<fetched>Z.<json|xml|html>.gz
stations/status.json      {provider/station: last_fetch_ok, newest_obs_utc, rows, error}

An e-mail goes out once per station and day when its newest observation is older than 6 h.

Provider Format Window Clock Avalanche Canada JSON ~7 days UTC offset in the string Whistler Blackcomb XML current values America/Vancouver Mike Wiegele (Mt St Anne) HTML table 26 h fixed UTC−7 (Etc/GMT+7), no year in the rows

Time zones

The worker's tzdata (2026e) keeps America/Edmonton at UTC−6 and America/Vancouver at UTC−7 all year from Nov 2026. The Mt St Anne clock was checked against the shortwave signal (sunrise/sunset) and is a fixed UTC−7. Do time-zone work on the worker, not with an older local tzdata.

docs.title: 7.2 Patching: smet_stations.py + configs/stations_v1.yaml
docs.text:
Per station and field, the donors are tried in order, hour by hour; the first valid value wins:

  1. station observation (raw archive, plus with --live the provider's current window),
  2. hrdps = the corrected series of the nearest 2.5 km cell (all within 1.6 km).

A donor at another altitude is moved to the station: TA/RH with the same lapse rates (RH_METHOD=fixed), PSUM by +5 % per 100 m. ISWR/ILWR come from HRDPS unless the station measures them. The forecast is HRDPS only.

QC (values outside → missing): TA −45…40 °C, RH 5…100 %, VW 0…40 m/s, DW 0…360°, PSUM 0…50 mm, ISWR 0…1400, ILWR 100…550 W/m². RH < 5 % counts as a sensor fault (Fidelity reports 0).

Station Operation Elev. From the station From HRDPS Fidelity Rogers Pass 1905 m TA, RH, wind, precipitation (RH = 0 fails QC → HRDPS) radiation Bosworth lower Banff 2210 m TA, RH (then Bosworth upper, 2745 m); wind from Bosworth upper precipitation, radiation Bow Summit Banff 2040 m TA, RH wind, precipitation, radiation Lookout Banff 2640 m TA, RH, wind precipitation, radiation Whistler Rendezvous Whistler 1920 m TA, RH (Rendezvous); wind (Horstman Hut, 2180 m); precipitation (Catskinner, 1550 m) radiation Mt St Anne MWHS 1900 m TA, wind, ISWR, ILWR (CM3 / CG3) RH (sensor fault), precipitation (gauge does not catch snow)

The manifest lists, per station and field, how many hours came from each donor.

docs.title: 8. Weather values for the dashboard
docs.text:
pipeline/geojson_extras.py runs after atoolchain and adds weather.* to every feature of <node>/geojson/<stamp>.<aspect>.json. Values cover the 24 h ending at the file's time; a failure is logged, not fatal.

Key Unit From hn24, hn48 cm SNOWPACK HN24 of the feature's slope, repaired at restart rows (below) rain24 mm SNOWPACK MS_Rain of the slope vw24, dw24, dw24_sector km/h, ° forcing wind (flat), vector mean weighted by speed gust24 km/h max hourly HRDPS gust, median over the location's cells ta, z °C, m forcing TA at the time step and its altitude snowline m elevation where the wet-bulb temperature (Stull) is +1 °C, TA/RH moved with the monthly lapse rates; precipitation-weighted mean if ≥ 1 mm fell, else median; semi-distributed bands take their region's BTL value snlvl m MSC snow level, median of the location's cells and hours

HN24 at the daily restart

The daily SNOWPACK resume at 06Z writes a record with every HN* / MS_* at 0, so AWSOME's own hn24 is 0 at every past 06Z. weather.hn24 repairs it as HN24(t+3h) − HN3(t+3h) + HN3(t−21h).

docs.title: 9. Script map
docs.text: Script Runs Reads Writes ingest/nwp_fetch.py hourly Datamart raw/<model>/… ingest/nwp_check.py daily raw/ manifests alert e-mail ingest/stations_fetch.py hourly provider pages raw/stations/…, stations/status.json pipeline/hrdps_correct.py daily (--pending) raw/hrdps, cell list corrected/hrdps/…_cells.nc, _gust.nc pipeline/lapse.py library — monthly lapse rates, SMET formatting pipeline/snlvl_fetch.py daily Datamart WEonG corrected/hrdps/…_snlvl.nc pipeline/smet_hex_v2.py daily corrected cells, hexagons hex SMETs pipeline/smet_grid.py daily corrected cells grid SMETs, cells.geojson pipeline/smet_stations.py daily corrected cells, raw/stations station SMETs pipeline/geojson_extras.py daily snowpack.zarr, gust, snow level weather.* in the geojson

docs.title: V. xsnow
docs.text:
Last updated: 25 Nov 2026

xsnow is AWSOME's xarray-based package for SNOWPACK output. It ships with the AWSOME install (code/snow-cover/postprocessing/xsnow) and turns the raw snowpack.zarr into one labelled dataset per node, xsnowpack.zarr. Every later step reads it: the stability indices, PWL, datetags, the profile viewer (nivix), and AvAPro v3.

docs.title: 1. Where it sits
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  SNP["SNOWPACK<br/>ZarrIO plugin"] --> SZ[("snowpack.zarr<br/>raw output, height in cm")]
  SZ -->|atoolchain step<br/>xsnowpack| XZ[("xsnowpack.zarr<br/>xsnow dataset")]
  XZ --> IDX["indices · pwl · datetags"]
  XZ --> SIM["simplified.zarr<br/>dashboard API"]
  XZ --> NV["nivix xserver<br/>profile viewer"]
  XZ --> AV["AvAPro v3"]
  SZ --> GX["geojson_extras.py<br/>HN*, MS_Rain, forcing"]

Figure 1. xsnow between SNOWPACK and the consumers of the profiles.

  • Recipe section: xsnowpack: {chunks: profile}.
  • In the daily resume, xsnow appends the new nowcast to the season dataset; the forecast hours follow on the same time axis.
  • Pinned to branch feat/adashboard (atoolchain imports ZarrTailSlopeMismatch from xsnow.io.zarr, which only that branch has; tags v1.0.0 and v1.1.0 are older). Switch back to dev/main once it is merged there.

docs.title: 2. Structure of xsnowpack.zarr
docs.text:
Dimension Content location model points (R1_ALP, W_0001_0017, Fidelity, …) with coords latitude, longitude, altitude time naive UTC, 3-hourly at 00, 03, …, 21 after a first step at 01:00; season + 48 h forecast slope coords inclination, azimuth: flat + 38° at 0/90/180/270 (stations also 45/135/225/315) realization 1 (deterministic) layer layer 0 = bottom snow element (no soil), surface = n_layers − 1, NaN padding above

Example sizes: banff_hex 12 × 419 × 5 × 1 × 23; Whistler up to 123 layers.

Select by coordinate, never by index

The slope order is not guaranteed. Use ds.sel(slope=...) on inclination / azimuth. region_id and band are not coords in the store: take them from atoolchain's <node>/locations.json (location id → band, region_id, elev, lon, lat).

docs.title: 3. Variables
docs.text:
Layer variablesProfile variables Variable Unit Note height m vertical height above ground of the layer top, on every slope density kg m⁻³ grain_type Swiss F1F2F3 code grain_size mm temperature °C lwc fraction liquid water content shear_strength Pa rta, ssi – SNOWPACK's own RTA (use directly) deposition_date datetime minute resolution (~13 µs jitter); merged elements keep the upper date datetag datetime mostly NaT; filled by the datetags step rc_flat, sk38, punstable, sk38_ccl, sk38_ccl_rta – from the indices step pwl flags – from the pwl step Variable Unit Note HS m snow depth SWE kg m⁻² equal across flat and 38° slopes n_layers – number of valid layers HN3, HN6, HN12, HN24, HN72_24 m new snow sums MS_Snow, MS_Rain kg m⁻² s⁻¹ / kg m⁻² h⁻¹ mass fluxes VW, VW_drift, wind_trans24 m s⁻¹, cm VW_drift ≡ VW, wind_trans24 ≡ 0 (no drift modelled)

hardness is absent from all 12 stores.

docs.title: 4. Checks done on the stores
docs.text: Check Result Heights vertical or slope-normal? Vertical. SNOWPACK writes (z + u − z_soil) / cos(slope); xsnow is a pass-through (snowpack.zarr height / 100 = xsnowpack.zarr height, max |Δ| 1.2e-7 m). height[n_layers−1] / HS = 1.0000 on every slope; HS(38°)/HS(flat) ≈ 1.01–1.03 at first snow, not 0.79. Mass consistency Σ ρ · Δh (vertical Δh) = SWE exactly; SWE equal on all slopes (e.g. 393.5 / 393.6 / 393.2 / 392.2 / 392.5 kg m⁻²). Slope-normal values build them once: height_n = height × cos(inclination) (flat: × 1).

docs.title: 5. Quirks
docs.text: Quirk Effect Handling 06 UTC restart dump atoolchain restarts SNOWPACK daily; the first output of each run (06 UTC) is the state plus one step, and the hazard data are not dumped: HN*, MS_*, wind_trans24 = 0 there. Layers, HS, SWE and dates are valid. geojson_extras.py repairs hn24; AvAPro v3 rebuilds HN3/6/12/24 from the flat profile's layers with SNOWPACK's own rule HN72_24 = HN24 in restart segments the 72 h buffer restarts with each run do not use as a 3-day sum No drift SNOW_EROSION and SNOW_REDISTRIBUTION off wind-slab detection uses wind speed + surface grains, not drift Irregular Δt first step 01:00, then 3-hourly read Δt from the data; windows are durations No forecast flag nowcast and forecast share the time axis build the mask from date_opera (<day>T06)

docs.title: 6. Reading a store
